correctness.rationale: For every field k, n≥2, and radical matrix X of rank r, column-wise and row-wise independent triangular multiplications give dim XT = sum of upper-left corner ranks and dim TX = sum of lower-right corner ranks. Each leading rank is at most min(r,j−1), and each trailing rank at least max(r−i+1,0), proving sharp bound r(n−r−1). Equality forces nonzero first r superdiagonal pivots and all rows below r zero, which also suffice. Their free coordinates give (G_m)^r × A^{rn−r(r+3)/2}; transpose-reflection exchanges signs. A rank-preserving sequence of nonattacking rook shifts reduces the gap by exactly one at each step and reaches the opposite bound, proving the entire spectrum. The script check.py exhaustively confirms 13 field-size examples incl. GF(4). Finite checks alone are not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: A directly relevant prior full text, Rahimi-Alangi–Yahaghi (2015), Corollary 2.5, already yields the principal one-sided ideal rank-profile formulas. These are explicitly credited, not claimed as new. Their Theorem 2.6 classifies principal nest modules but does not determine the maximal or possible differences of left and right ideal dimensions at fixed matrix rank, their sharp equality conditions, or extremal finite-field matrix counts. Older superclass-orbit and Jordan-rank tables address related but different invariants. Novelty is claimed only for this joint rank-conditioned extremal/attainability theorem, with a substantial residual risk of indirect derivation from the prior nest-module theory.
residual_risks: Rahimi-Alangi–Yahaghi (2015) already contains the one-sided rank-profile identity, so any originality priority is restricted to the sharp joint fixed-rank gap, attainability and equality counts. These could be implicit consequences of their principal nest-module framework and need independent review.
The superclass/rook framework may imply the extremal law after an unstated but nontrivial specialization. No absolute novelty certification is claimed.
Other literature on one-sided rank profiles or triangular matrix modules could contain equivalent statements under different names.

value.rationale: The one-sided principal ideals of a radical element are intrinsic modules whose dimension imbalance quantifies the noncommutative orientation asymmetry in a standard hereditary algebra. The theorem supplies a field-independent sharp quadratic bound, every attainable signed value at each ordinary rank, and all endpoint algebraic loci with exact finite-field cardinality, rather than an arbitrary finite example or marginal matrix-rank count. These natural extremal and geometric data can guide comparisons for incidence and pattern algebras.
